fact: Neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) affect an estimated 2.7 billion of the world's poorest people, causing significant physical debilitation, lowered economic productivity, and social ostracism.
source_span: Neglected tropical diseases ( NTDs ) are parasitic and bacterial diseases that affect an estimated 2 . 7 billion of the world's poorest people , causing significant physical debilitation , lowered economic productivity , and social ostracism for afflicted individuals [1] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the global burden and importance of NTDs, motivating the study.

fact: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy—lymphatic filariasis (LF), trachoma, schistosomiasis, onchocerciasis, and soil-transmitted helminths (STH)—have been targeted for control or elimination.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy: lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis , onchocerciasis and the three soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) ; have been targeted for control or elimination , but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2] .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines the diseases targeted by control programs and frames the study's disease focus.

fact: Resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward control and elimination goals for NTDs.
source_span: Five NTDs with available preventive chemotherapy ... have been targeted for control or elimination , but resource constraints in endemic countries have impeded progress toward these goals [2] .
selection_reasoning: This highlights the problem motivating the development of more efficient mapping methods.

fact: Mass drug administration (MDA) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs is the core public health strategy to fight the five targeted NTDs.
source_span: At the core of public health efforts to fight the five NTDs mentioned above is a strategy of mass drug administration ( MDA ) of at-risk populations with safe and effective drugs often donated by pharmaceutical companies [5] .
selection_reasoning: This explains the main intervention approach relevant to the study.

fact: Before launching MDA, countries must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention, as established by WHO, has been surpassed.
source_span: Before an MDA can be launched , a country must demonstrate that the disease threshold for public health intervention , as established by the World Health Organization ( WHO ) , has been surpassed [6] , [7] .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains why mapping and threshold determination are critical.

fact: Currently, each NTD program uses its own mapping methodology, which can be costly and burdensome when multiple surveys are needed in the same country.
source_span: Currently , each NTD program has its own methodology [8] . Conducting multiple surveys in the same country can be costly and burdensome to national disease programs .
selection_reasoning: This motivates the need for an integrated mapping approach.

fact: Because NTDs tend to overlap geographically, an integrated mapping approach could result in significant resource savings and more efficient identification of populations needing treatment.
source_span: Because NTDs tend to overlap in geographic areas , it is logical that an integrated approach to mapping NTDs might result in more efficient identification of populations needing treatment [9] .
selection_reasoning: This provides the rationale for developing an integrated mapping protocol.

fact: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology for lymphatic filariasis, trachoma, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: We developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ( ITM ) Methodology ) for lymphatic filariasis ( LF ) , trachoma , schistosomiasis and soil-transmitted helminths ( STH ) .
selection_reasoning: This states the main methodological innovation of the study.

fact: The ITM protocol is designed to be resource-efficient and aims to determine whether a disease has reached the threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit.
source_span: The protocol is designed to be resource-efficient , and its specific purpose is to determine whether a threshold to trigger public health interventions in an implementation unit has been attained .
selection_reasoning: This clarifies the purpose and advantage of the ITM protocol.

fact: The ITM protocol relies on WHO-recommended indicators in disease-specific age groups and uses the district as the sampling frame, except for schistosomiasis where the sub-district is used.
source_span: The protocol relies on World Health Organization ( WHO ) recommended indicators in the disease-specific age groups . For each disease , the sampling frame was the district , but for schistosomiasis , the sub-district rather than the ecological zone was used .
selection_reasoning: This describes the high-level design of the ITM protocol relevant to its validity.

fact: The ITM methodology was field-tested by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies in one district each in Mali and Senegal.
source_span: We tested the protocol by comparing it to current WHO mapping methodologies for each of the targeted diseases in one district each in Mali and Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This states the key validation approach used in the study.

fact: The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis, and soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as the WHO methodologies regarding the initiation of public health interventions for trachoma , LF and STH ...
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding supporting the validity of the ITM approach.

fact: The ITM methodology resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: In this study , the ITM methodology ... resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis .
selection_reasoning: This highlights a key difference and potential advantage of the ITM method.

fact: The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings compared with the standard, non-integrated WHO methodologies.
source_span: ITM was practical , feasible and demonstrated an overall cost saving compared with the standard , non-integrated , WHO methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact supports the significance and potential impact of the ITM approach.

fact: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed NTD programs in endemic countries.
source_span: This integrated mapping tool could facilitate the implementation of much-needed programs in endemic countries .
selection_reasoning: This states the translational significance and potential public health impact.

fact: Trachoma was assessed by examining children aged 1-9 years for active trachoma and females aged 15 years and older for trichiasis using the WHO Simplified Grading System.
source_span: For trachoma , an ophthalmic technician examined both eyes of children aged 1?? years for clinical signs of active trachoma ( trachomatous inflammation follicular [TF] ) and of females aged ??5 years for clinical signs of trichiasis ( trachomatous trichiasis [TT] ) using a binocular loupe and natural light according to the WHO Simplified Grading System [12] .
selection_reasoning: This background fact explains the disease assessment method and population, which is core to understanding the study's approach to trachoma.

fact: Schistosoma haematobium infection was detected by testing for haematuria in urine samples from children aged 6-9 years using urine reagent strips.
source_span: For Schistosoma haematobium , the presence of haematuria in urine samples from children aged 6?? years was detected by urine reagent strips .
selection_reasoning: This fact describes a key diagnostic method for schistosomiasis, relevant to the study's disease mapping.

fact: The prevalence and egg load of Schistosoma mansoni and soil-transmitted helminths (STH) were measured using the Kato-Katz method.
source_span: For Schistosoma mansoni and STH , the prevalence and egg load ( eggs per gram of feces ) were calculated using the Kato-Katz method [14] .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a high-level description of how key parasitic infections were measured, important for understanding the study methods.

fact: Children found to have active trachoma were treated with tetracycline ointment applied twice daily for six weeks.
source_span: Children who were found to have active trachoma received two tubes of tetracycline ointment , to be applied twice daily for a period of six weeks .
selection_reasoning: This fact states a clinical intervention linked to the study findings, relevant for translational significance.

fact: Females with trichiasis were referred to health centers for trichiasis surgery.
source_span: Females found to have trichiasis were referred to the nearest health center that provides trichiasis surgery .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a clinical follow-up action based on disease detection, important for public health relevance.

fact: Persons testing positive for Wuchereria bancrofti antigen and children infected with Schistosoma haematobium, Schistosoma mansoni, or soil-transmitted helminths were referred to district health centers if mass drug administration (MDA) was not planned.
source_span: Persons who tested positive for W . bancrofti antigen and children who were found to be infected with S . haematobium , S . mansoni or STH were referred to the district health center in case an MDA was not planned in the district .
selection_reasoning: This fact connects diagnostic results to public health interventions, relevant for the study's translational impact.

fact: The study compared two methodologies, the ITM and WHO methods, for mapping neglected tropical diseases including trachoma, schistosomiasis, soil-transmitted helminths, and lymphatic filariasis.
source_span: Results for trachoma , STH and LF were analyzed at the district level for both methodologies ... Results for schistosomiasis were calculated at the sub-district level for the ITM methodology and at the ecological zone level for the WHO methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes the main comparative approach of the study, central to the research question.

fact: In Banamba District, Mali, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated no need for mass drug administration (MDA) for trachoma or soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: As shown in Figure 3 , the results of both methodologies indicated no need for MDA for trachoma ( ITM Method: 1 . 9% , WHO method: 4 . 7% , 95% CI: 2 . 9?? . 5 or STH: 0% , 0% ) within the surveyed district .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports a principal finding about disease prevalence and intervention need, key to the study conclusions.

fact: Both methodologies agreed on the need for trichiasis surgeries in Banamba District, Mali.
source_span: The methodologies were also concordant in indicating a need for TT surgeries ( ITM Method: 2 . 6% , WHO Method: 3 . 7% , 95% CI: 2 . 4?? . 1 ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights agreement between methods on a key public health intervention.

fact: The ITM and WHO methodologies differed in schistosomiasis treatment recommendations in Banamba District, with the ITM method identifying more sub-districts needing mass drug administration for the whole population.
source_span: Because the ITM method had as its purpose to refine the schistosomiasis mapping , the two methods differed , in indicating a need for schistosomiasis treatment: the WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis among only school-aged children in the entire area . The ITM methodology indicated that four sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , and that five sub-districts were in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population .
selection_reasoning: This fact captures a key difference in mapping outcomes affecting treatment scope, central to the study's significance.

fact: Treating the whole population in sub-districts identified by the ITM method would result in nearly 33,500 additional at-risk persons being treated compared to treating only school-aged children as indicated by the WHO method.
source_span: Treating the whole population in the sub-districts where this was indicated by the integrated mapping protocol would result in nearly 33 , 500 additional at-risk persons being treated than if only school-aged children in these sub-districts were treated ( as indicated by the WHO protocol ) .
selection_reasoning: This fact quantifies the public health impact of the differing mapping methodologies, important for policy implications.

fact: In Diourbel District, Senegal, both ITM and WHO methodologies indicated the need for mass drug administration for trachoma but no need for intervention for soil-transmitted helminths.
source_span: Both methodologies indicated the need for MDA for trachoma in the surveyed district ( ITM Method: 14 . 9% , WHO Method: 13 . 4% , 95% CI: 9 . 8??7 . 0 ) and both methodologies indicated that there was no need for intervention for STH: 0% , 0% .
selection_reasoning: This fact reports concordant findings on disease prevalence and intervention need in a second study site.

fact: Both ITM and WHO methodologies agreed on the need for trichiasis surgeries in Diourbel District, Senegal.

selection_reasoning: This fact highlights consistent agreement on a key clinical intervention across methods and sites.

fact: The lymphatic filariasis (LF) mapping was included to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping approach rather than to validate disease prevalence results.
source_span: The LF mapping was added to validate the feasibility of the integrated mapping and not to validate the results .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies the purpose of including LF mapping, relevant to understanding study design and scope.

fact: The Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) methodology is an operational tool designed for Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold for launching disease-specific public health interventions has been reached.
source_span: We describe an integrated NTD mapping methodology ( Integrated Threshold Mapping ) that can be used as an operational tool by Ministries of Health in NTD-endemic countries to determine if the threshold needed to launch disease-specific public health intervenions has been reached .
selection_reasoning: This fact introduces the main method developed in the study and its intended use, which is central to the article's purpose.

fact: The ITM methodology balances epidemiologic rigour with field practicality to provide a simpler and quicker way for Ministries of Health to estimate their neglected tropical disease (NTD) needs.
source_span: In developing this ITM methodology , we sought to balance epidemiologic rigour with field practicality , resulting in an approach that can be used only for determining where public health interventions are needed .
selection_reasoning: This explains the motivation and design principle behind the ITM method, important for understanding its significance.

fact: The ITM methodology retains key indicators and age groups from WHO disease-specific mapping guidelines but adapts the sampling methodologies to improve practicality.
source_span: With the exception of some minor modifications for trachoma , we have retained the key indicators and age groups used in the disease-specific WHO mapping guidelines , but have adapted the sampling methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies how the ITM method relates to existing WHO protocols, which is important for context and acceptance.

fact: The ITM methodology reduces costs, manpower, and resource needs compared to the WHO methodology, providing overall cost savings of 31% in Mali and 19% in Senegal.
source_span: The results of the cost data analysis Table 4 , indicate that using the ITM methodology resulted in a 31% overall cost savings in Mali ( $6 , 968 vs . $10 , 039 ) , and a 19% overall cost savings in Senegal ( $8 , 442 vs . $10 , 372 ) .
selection_reasoning: Cost savings and resource efficiency are key findings demonstrating the practical benefits of the ITM method.

fact: The ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in travel, supplies, and team training in both Mali and Senegal.
source_span: In both countries , the ITM methodology used resources more efficiently than the WHO methodology in the areas of travel , supplies and team training , as shown in Table 4 .
selection_reasoning: This supports the significance of the ITM method's efficiency, reinforcing its advantage over the WHO method.

fact: In Mali, the ITM methodology identified more sub-districts needing mass drug administration (MDA) for schistosomiasis than the WHO methodology, targeting nearly 46,000 extra at-risk individuals for treatment.
source_span: The WHO methodology indicated a need for MDA for schistosomiasis treatment among only school-aged children in the entire area , while the ITM methodology indicated six sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis among school-aged children only , four sub-districts in need of MDA for schistosomiasis for the whole population and one sub-district which did not pass the threshold for treatment . Compared to the district based WHO protocol , the ITM methodology targeted nearly 46 , 000 extra at-risk individuals for treatment .
selection_reasoning: This is a principal finding showing how the ITM method can affect public health intervention decisions.

fact: The ITM methodology uses program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO, with minor adaptations for trachoma, to allow application of WHO thresholds and reduce the number of people undergoing multiple tests.
source_span: In our ITM mapping protocol , we insisted on using the program-specific age groups as indicated by WHO with the exception of some adaptation for trachoma . The advantage of using these established age groups was that the WHO thresholds were applicable and that few people had to undergo multiple tests and examinations; only in a limited number of cases were people asked to undergo more than one test or examination .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key methodological choice that supports the validity and practicality of the ITM approach.

fact: The ITM methodology uses convenience sampling in villages to facilitate data collection and improve time efficiency compared to house-to-house visits used in the WHO trachoma protocol.
source_span: In each village , we chose to use a convenience sample for reasons of field practicality . Asking people of different ages to come to a central location in each village facilitated data collection and was much more time-efficient than house-to-house visits , such as those used in the WHO trachoma protocol .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights a key adaptation in sampling that improves field practicality, relevant to the method's significance.

fact: Field testing in Mali and Senegal showed that the ITM and WHO methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations for neglected tropical diseases.
source_span: As the field testing in both countries showed , the data of both methodologies resulted in the same public health recommendations .
selection_reasoning: This finding supports the validity of the ITM method in guiding public health decisions.

fact: The ITM protocol is not designed to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data or to serve as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level.
source_span: To understand the value and limitations of this protocol , it is critical to understand that this protocol is not claiming to provide epidemiologically correct prevalence data because both the villages and the individuals tested were not randomly selected . First , this implies that we cannot recommend using findings from this methodology as a baseline for measuring impact at the district level .
selection_reasoning: This limitation is important for interpreting the scope and appropriate use of the ITM method.

fact: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for lymphatic filariasis, schistosomiasis, and soil-transmitted helminths but uses a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation.
source_span: The ITM protocol maintains the WHO-recommended disease indicators and thresholds for LF , schistosomiasis and STH , but we used a novel sampling frame for more practical field implementation .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the study's methodological innovation while preserving standard disease metrics, which is central to understanding the study's approach.

fact: To improve representativeness for the trachomatous inflammation—follicular (TF) indicator, the study selected a predetermined number of children aged 1 to 6 years to prevent biased prevalence estimates.
source_span: To improve the representativeness for the TF indicator , we selected a pre-determined number of children between the ages of 1?? and 6?? . This was intended to prevent biased estimates in case the 6?? year age group made up the majority of children being graded for trachoma because prevalence rates are highest in 1?? year olds .
selection_reasoning: This fact clarifies a key sampling decision to ensure accurate disease prevalence measurement, relevant to the study's validity.

fact: The study used women above the age of 15 years to measure trachomatous trichiasis prevalence, based on expert consultation and literature review.
source_span: After consultation with trachoma experts , we decided to use women above the age of 15 yrs [22] .
selection_reasoning: This fact defines a key demographic choice for measuring a critical disease indicator, important for interpreting results.

fact: The ITM methodology links the sampling frame directly to the implementation unit for mass drug administration (MDA) for each neglected tropical disease to improve public health action feasibility.
source_span: Because the ITM methodology is focused on public health action , the sampling frame is directly linked to the implementation unit for MDA for each of the NTDs .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the practical public health focus of the methodology, a core motivation and significance.

fact: The study used the district as the primary implementation unit for soil-transmitted helminths, lymphatic filariasis, and trachoma, following WHO recommendations and to facilitate large-scale program implementation.
source_span: Because a village-centered approach is difficult for implementation and supervision for a large-scale national program , we decided to use the district as the primary implementation unit for STH as it is recommended by WHO for LF and trachoma .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains a key organizational decision affecting intervention delivery, relevant to the study's design and findings.

fact: The integrated methodology and WHO methodology agreed that no intervention was necessary for soil-transmitted helminths in the two countries studied.
source_span: Our methodology found the same public health intervention for trachoma and for STH . For STH , both methodologies concluded that no intervention was necessary , which confirmed the reliability of our methodology in the two countries .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides a principal finding validating the new methodology against the WHO standard.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the study recommends using sub-district implementation units for MDA to better target treatment and avoid overtreating or undertreating subpopulations.
source_span: In the case of schistosomiasis , a disease that is very focal in nature , and for which treatment medication is costly and in limited supply , we feel that it would be more appropriate to use the sub-district as implementation units to determine needs for treatment because a district-based approach may result in overtreating or undertreating subpopulations within the district [23] .
selection_reasoning: This fact addresses a key disease-specific recommendation with clinical and public health significance.

fact: Using the sub-district as the implementation unit for schistosomiasis allowed the integrated methodology to identify highly endemic and low endemic sub-areas within districts that the WHO ecological zone approach missed.
source_span: Our results show that by using the sub-district as I . U . , the MDA will be more targeted to people at risk . In our study , when the WHO-recommended ecological zone was used as the implementation unit , highly endemic ( prevalence of >50% ) or low endemic ( prevalence of <10% ) sub-areas of the district were not identified , but were identified by the integrated methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact demonstrates a key advantage of the integrated approach in targeting treatment more precisely.

fact: Using the WHO protocol for schistosomiasis would have resulted in undertreating tens of thousands of people in highly endemic areas and overtreating others not in need of treatment, as shown in Senegal.
source_span: As a result , using the WHO protocol would have meant that tens of thousands of people living in highly endemic areas would not have received treatment , and that other people not in need of treatment would have been treated , as would have been the case in Senegal .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the public health risk of the current WHO protocol and the significance of the integrated method.

fact: The integrated approach was more efficient in cost, transport, time in the field, and use of human resources compared to the WHO methodologies.
source_span: The integrated approach proved to be more efficient in cost , transport , time in the field and the use of human resources .
selection_reasoning: This fact summarizes a principal finding about the practical benefits of the integrated methodology.

fact: The integrated mapping team used one vehicle and five experienced technicians performing multiple tasks, compared to the WHO methodology which used three vehicles and seven team members.
source_span: The ITM methodology used one vehicle to transport the team , versus 3 used in the WHO methodologies , employed a 5-member team instead of a 7-member team , and took about half as much time to implement as the WHO methodologies .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides concrete evidence of resource efficiency, supporting the significance claim.

fact: Cost savings from integrated mapping include reduced planning and logistic preparations, which is valuable for overburdened health staff.
source_span: It is also important to mention that certain cost savings from integrated mapping such as time saved by only having to plan one survey compared with several different protocol meetings and logistic preparations is priceless for overburdened health staff .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains an important practical advantage of integration relevant to health system capacity.

fact: Mapping is often the first field activity of an integrated neglected tropical disease program, and integrated surveys help demonstrate the concept of integrating vertical programs at all levels of the Ministry of Health.
source_span: mapping is often the first field activity of an integrated NTD program , and the creation of the team demonstrated the concept of integrating vertical programs to all levels of the MoH and this first activity can help with further collaboration for implementing integrated public health interventions .
selection_reasoning: This fact highlights the broader significance of integrated mapping beyond cost savings.

fact: Although the ITM methodology resulted in substantial cost savings compared to the WHO methodology, the cost depends on the number of sub-units in a district, which can increase sampling size for schistosomiasis.
source_span: Although the ITM methodology resulted in substantial cost savings compared to the WHO methodology , the cost depends on the number of sub-units in a district . This means , for example , that the sampling size for schistosomiasis could be much higher using the ITM methodology than using the WHO methodology .
selection_reasoning: This fact qualifies the cost advantage by noting a trade-off important for interpreting the findings.

fact: A more targeted mass drug administration for schistosomiasis is important because donated praziquantel medication is limited in availability.
source_span: However , this would result in a more targeted MDA for schistosomiasis , which is important because there is limited availability of donated praziquantel .
selection_reasoning: This fact explains the clinical and public health importance of targeting treatment accurately.

fact: Health workers are not always well-informed about where schistosomiasis is most prevalent, as indicated by the study results.
source_span: The results from both the ITM and WHO methologies indicate that health workers are not always well-informed about where schistosomiasis is most prevalent .
selection_reasoning: This fact provides motivation for improved mapping methods to guide treatment.

fact: This study presents a novel integrated mapping protocol to determine whether thresholds for public health interventions for neglected tropical diseases have been reached.
source_span: This study shows a novel integrated mapping protocol to determine whether thresholds for public health interventions have been reached.
selection_reasoning: Introducing the main methodological innovation central to the study's purpose and findings.

fact: The integrated mapping approach is logistically practical, cost-efficient, and flexible for mapping neglected tropical diseases.
source_span: The approach is logistically practical , cost-efficient and flexible .
selection_reasoning: Highlights key advantages of the new method relevant to its potential adoption and impact.

fact: For schistosomiasis, the integrated mapping approach results in more targeted mass drug administrations compared with the district-level implementation currently used by most integrated NTD programs.
source_span: For schistosomiasis , our approach also results in more targeted MDAs compared with the district level implementation currently adapted by most integrated NTD program .
selection_reasoning: Describes a principal finding showing improved intervention targeting, which is a key outcome.

fact: The protocol mainly uses age-specific disease indicators as recommended by the World Health Organization.
source_span: The protocol uses mainly the age-specific disease indicators as recommended by WHO .
selection_reasoning: Specifies the biological and measurement basis of the method, important for understanding how it works.

fact: The integrated mapping protocol lays the foundation for subsequent integrated program activities essential for neglected tropical disease elimination and control.
source_span: Further , it sets the stage for all of the following integrated program activities essential for NTD elimination and control .
selection_reasoning: Indicates the broader significance and application of the method beyond initial mapping.

fact: The study identified selection bias in some villages because up to 62% of the sample was selected by convenience rather than random sampling.
source_span: for the other six villages , a selection bias was likely introduced because up to 62% of the sample was selected by convenience only and those persons would maybe not have been included if the sample was collected randomly .
selection_reasoning: Acknowledges a key limitation affecting data quality and interpretation, relevant for understanding study validity.

fact: To reduce the burden on inhabitants, the study combined data from integrated mapping with additional household visits rather than examining the same children twice.
source_span: To decrease the burden of the inhabitants by not having the same children examined twice , we included the data collected in the integrated mapping for the WHO method and added only 30 children by visiting the households .
selection_reasoning: Describes an important methodological consideration balancing data collection and participant burden.

fact: Based on lessons learned and feedback, the integrated mapping approach is being modified and field tested with all villages selected randomly to improve data usefulness.
source_span: For this reason , we are currently field testing an adapted protocol with all villages selected randomly among other minor changes .
selection_reasoning: Indicates ongoing refinement of the method to address limitations and improve future application.
